best_for: Anyone with a folder of odd video files, DVDs or network streams who wants one free player that opens them without hunting for codec packs.
description:
VLC media player is a free player and media framework from VideoLAN, a nonprofit organization. It is open source under the GPL.

VLC uses your graphics chip to decode video when it can, and falls back to the processor when it cannot. It reads subtitle files in many formats and lets you shift them earlier or later when they do not line up with the speech. You can adjust the picture and sound with video and audio filters. It also tunes in to digital TV, satellite and cable sources through a DVB card, and opens streams over HTTP, FTP, RTP and UDP, so a network video plays like a local file.

points.title: Plays almost anything as is
points.text: VLC handles MPEG-2, H.264, MKV, MP3 and many other formats without extra codec packs, plus DVDs, audio CDs, VCDs, webcams and network streams.

points.title: No ads and no tracking
points.text: VideoLAN states the player has no spyware, no ads and no user tracking. It is open source under the GPL and costs nothing.

points.title: Runs on very old systems
points.text: VideoLAN says the current version runs on Windows from XP SP3 to Windows 11 and on Mac OS X 10.7.5 or later. Older releases for even older Macs are kept on its site, back to PowerPC builds.

points.title: Every Windows package type
points.text: Windows gets .exe and .msi installers plus zip archives, each in 32-bit, 64-bit and ARM64. The .msi suits admins who deploy software. This site keeps 15 Windows versions.

points.title: Separate Intel and Apple silicon builds
points.text: On macOS you can pick an Intel build, an Apple silicon build or a universal one. First-generation Intel Core Solo and Core Duo Macs are no longer supported by current versions.

points.title: Linux: a community Flatpak
points.text: The Flatpak listed here, for x64 and ARM64, is not verified on Flathub. macOS and Linux list only the current release here.
